---
title: "How to extract raw snippets to send to the IBL"
---

This guide is for labs that share Neuropixels recordings with the IBL. The recordings are too
large to move, so you run one command per probe. It reads your SpikeGLX recording, keeps five
short snippets of the raw AP and LF data, adds the probe geometry and (optionally) your
histology, and writes one `.h5` file that you send to us. Nothing is filtered or otherwise
processed, so we can try different analyses without asking you for more data.

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.12 or newer
- A SpikeGLX recording of the probe: the `.ap.bin` or `.ap.cbin` file with its `.meta` file
  next to it. The `.lf.bin` / `.lf.cbin` file is used when it is next to the AP file.
- Supported probes: Neuropixels 1.0, 3A and 2.x (including four-shank 2.4). Neuropixels 2
  records no separate LF band, so only the wideband data is stored and we compute LF
  ourselves. If your probe type is not supported, the command stops and says so; please tell
  us the probe type.

## Install

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/int-brain-lab/ibleatools@<tag>
```

Use the tag we gave you in place of `<tag>`. This installs ibleatools and its dependencies,
which is a large install.

## Extract the snippets

Run the command once per probe:

```bash
ibleatools-snippets /data/probe00/run_g0_t0.imec0.ap.cbin \
    -o /data/to_send/VF066_2025-12-04_probe00.h5 \
    --histology /data/VF066/alf/probe00/channel_locations.json /data/VF066/alf/probe00/xyz_picks.json \
    --trajectory 2243 -2000 -200 4000 15 180
```

- `-o` is the file to write. Name it so that you can tell the subject, date and probe apart;
  the command refuses to overwrite an existing file.
- `--histology` is optional. List the files or folders of this probe's histology, for example
  `channel_locations.json`, `xyz_picks.json` or the tracing CSVs. They are copied as they are.
  Only small per-probe files are accepted: the total is limited to 100 MB, so whole-brain
  image volumes are rejected.
- `--trajectory` is optional (the numbers above are only an example). It is the planned insertion, six numbers: `x y z depth theta phi`.
  Use the IBL Alyx convention: `x`, `y`, `z` in um relative to bregma (`x` is mediolateral,
  right positive; `y` is anterior-posterior, anterior positive; `z` is dorsoventral, dorsal
  positive), `depth` in um along the probe, `theta` (from straight up) and `phi` (from the +x
  axis) in degrees. If your lab uses other conventions, convert the numbers first.

By default the command takes 5 snippets of 5 s, spread over the recording and leaving out the
first and last 5 minutes. Options for other cases:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--t-starts 600 900` | Snippet start times in seconds, instead of automatic ones |
| `--n-snippets`, `--duration` | Number and length (s) of the automatic snippets |
| `--margin` | Seconds skipped at each end; lower it for recordings shorter than about 10 minutes |

`ibleatools-snippets --help` lists everything.

If a run fails, the command prints the reason and exits with a non-zero code, so a script
that loops over probes can check the exit code.

## What the file holds

- The raw AP and LF samples of each snippet, compressed without loss, with the gains to
  convert them to volts.
- The probe geometry, each channel's shank, the original `.meta` text, and the start time of
  each snippet in your recording.
- The histology files and the trajectory, if you passed them.

The SpikeGLX sync channel is not included. A Neuropixels 1.0 probe gives about 0.23 GB per
file with the defaults (5 snippets of 5 s).

## Send us the files

Send us the `.h5` files, for example zipped together. One file is written per probe, so
repeat the command for each probe of each session.
